pamphlet_excerpts: Stamp Collecting Sub-Req 1a: Discuss how you can better understand people, places, institutions, history, and geography as a result of collecting stamps.
Stamp Collecting Sub-Req 1b: Briefly describe some aspects of the history, growth, and development of the United States postal system. Tell how it is different from postal systems in other countries.
Core Standard 1 (Req 1): Do the following: (a) Discuss how you can better understand people, places, institutions, history, and geography as a result of collecting stamps.
Core Standard 2 (Req 1): (b) Briefly describe some aspects of the history, growth, and development of the United States postal system.
step_by_step_procedure: Prepare & Inspect (Req 1): Review the official Stamp Collecting requirement standard and verify all required tools, reference tables, and safety gear.
Analyze Core Principles: Identify the primary concepts, definitions, and cause-and-effect relationships governing (a) Discuss how you can better understand people.
Execute & Document: Perform the demonstrate task methodically with your patrol buddy and log specific observations in your Stamp Collecting Workbook.
Verify With Counselor: Present your completed work, demonstrate proficiency, and answer Socratic check-for-understanding questions for Blue Card sign-off.

Core Standard 1 (Req 4): Do the following: (a) Demonstrate the use of ONE standard catalog for several different stamp issues.
Core Standard 2 (Req 4): Explain why catalog value can vary from the corresponding purchase price.
step_by_step_procedure: Prepare & Inspect (Req 4): Review the official Stamp Collecting requirement standard and verify all required tools, reference tables, and safety gear.
Analyze Core Principles: Identify the primary concepts, definitions, and cause-and-effect relationships governing (a) Demonstrate the use of ONE standard catalog.
Execute & Document: Perform the demonstrate task methodically with your patrol buddy and log specific observations in your Stamp Collecting Workbook.
Verify With Counselor: Present your completed work, demonstrate proficiency, and answer Socratic check-for-understanding questions for Blue Card sign-off.

requirements.req_text: Do TWO of the following: (a) Design a stamp, cancellation, or cachet. (b) Visit a post office, stamp club, or stamp show with an experienced collector. Explain what you saw and learned. (c) Write a review of an interesting article from a stamp newspaper, magazine, book, or website (with your parent or guardian's permission). (d) Research and report on a famous stamp-related personality or the history behind a particular stamp. (e) Describe the steps taken to produce a stamp. Include the methods of printing, types of paper, perforation styles, and how they are gummed. (f) Prepare a two- to three-page display involving stamps. Using ingenuity, as well as clippings, drawings, etc., tell a story about the stamps and how they relate to history, geography, or a favorite topic of yours.

pamphlet_excerpts: Stamp Collecting Sub-Req 7a: Design a stamp, cancellation, or cachet.
Stamp Collecting Sub-Req 7b: Visit a post office, stamp club, or stamp show with an experienced collector. Explain what you saw and learned.
Stamp Collecting Sub-Req 7c: Write a review of an interesting article from a stamp newspaper, magazine, book, or website (with your parent or guardian's permission).
Stamp Collecting Sub-Req 7d: Research and report on a famous stamp-related personality or the history behind a particular stamp.
step_by_step_procedure: Prepare & Inspect (Req 7): Review the official Stamp Collecting requirement standard and verify all required tools, reference tables, and safety gear.
Analyze Core Principles: Identify the primary concepts, definitions, and cause-and-effect relationships governing (a) Design a stamp, cancellation, or cachet. (b).
Execute & Document: Perform the design task methodically with your patrol buddy and log specific observations in your Stamp Collecting Workbook.
Verify With Counselor: Present your completed work, demonstrate proficiency, and answer Socratic check-for-understanding questions for Blue Card sign-off.

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: During a patrol review of Stamp Collecting Requirement 7, a Scout claims: "Reading a short definition of (a) Design a stamp, cancellation, or cachet. (b) is enough for Stamp Collecting Requirement 7 sign-off." How should you respond?
options: Agree with the claim so the patrol can finish the requirement faster

Correct the misconception: Each Scout must actively design the specific principles and real-world steps of (a) Design a stamp, cancellation, or cachet. (b) grounded in the official Stamp Collecting pamphlet.
Skip Requirement 7 until after the troop court of honor
Sign off the Blue Card without completing the practical verification
quiz_item.correct_answer: Option B - Correct the misconception: Each Scout must actively design the specific principles and real-world steps of (a) Design a stamp, cancellation, or cachet. (b) grounded in the official Stamp Collecting pamphlet.
quiz_item.explanation: Per Official BSA Stamp Collecting Pamphlet, pp. 40-45, Each Scout must actively design the specific principles and real-world steps of (a) Design a stamp, cancellation, or cachet. (b) grounded in the official Stamp Collecting pamphlet.

requirements.lead_text: Mount and show, in a purchased or homemade album, ONE of the following:
requirements.req_text: Mount and show, in a purchased or homemade album, ONE of the following: (a) A collection of 250 or more different stamps from at least 15 countries (b) A collection of a stamp from each of 50 different countries, mounted on maps to show the location of each (c) A collection of 100 or more different stamps from either one country or a group of closely related countries (d) A collection of 75 or more different stamps on a single topic. (Some interesting topics include Scouting, birds, insects, the Olympics, sports, flowers, animals, ships, holidays, trains, famous people, space, and medicine.) Stamps may be from different countries. (e) A collection of postal items discovered in your mail by monitoring it over a period of 30 days. Include at least five different types listed in requirement 3.
